solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Monitors Number Six at first

parts.note: a number on an album is a track, one song or piece

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word Six

explanation.surface: Someone keeps watch over Number Six, as in the cult TV show The Prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something is to follow or keep watch on it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Putin heartily eggs on wealthy comrade

indicators.note: heartily asks for the heart, the central letter, of the name Putin

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: The Russian president urges on a rich ally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian word for comrade, used in Soviet times as a form of address.

clue.text: American male probing 46th vice-president, most dangerous opponent

indicators.note: probing means pushing into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Richard (R.) Cheney was the 46th US vice-president, under George W. Bush

explanation.surface: An American man investigates a former vice-president, his deadliest foe.
explanation.walkthrough: The vice-president needs his initial: R CHENEY, with M put inside after CHENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal enemy, the chief or worst adversary someone has.

clue.text: Kilts initially vex Scottish church

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word Kilts

parts.note: to vex is to irk or annoy

explanation.surface: Wearing kilts is irritating to the Scottish church at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for a church building or the Church of Scotland.

clue.text: Lug instrument round edges of tomato field

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O

indicators.note: edges of asks for the outer letters of the word tomato

parts.note: a field of activity is its scope or range

explanation.surface: A device for working round the edges of a tomato field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' is slang for the ear, not a verb meaning carry.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument doctors use to look into the ear canal; lug is informal for ear.

clue.text: They can be made from tansies

definitions.text: They can be made from tansies

indicators.note: can be made from says the letters of tansies are rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: Herbal drinks can be brewed from tansy, a garden herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal infusions, which can be brewed from tansy leaves among other plants.

clue.text: Very sweet bag lady who does feel sad to be penniless

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
a 'lady who does' is a British euphemism for a charwoman or cleaner, a char

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, and P stands for penny in British money

parts.note: to pine is to feel sad from longing

explanation.surface: A bag lady and her cleaner are miserable at having no money.
explanation.walkthrough: PINE loses its P to give INE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickly sweet, like the artificial sweetener of the same name.

clue.text: Has to break vows

indicators.note: break suggests the letters of 'Has to' are broken up and put back differently

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to break their promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn promises or sworn pledges, the plural noun in both.

clue.text: Student taking top off as way to make money

indicators.note: taking top off in a down clue means removing the first letter

parts.note: a student is a learner

explanation.surface: A student strips off a top as a way of making cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings in income, such as a nice little side job.

clue.text: Quarter of us enthralled by organ which is pink and hot

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper, and the Financial Times is printed on pink paper
of us means belonging to us, our
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A quarter of us are captivated by some pink and hot bodily organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'organ which is pink' is this very newspaper, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: One of four equal parts, a synonym for one quarter.

clue.text: Standing in for another girl needing dental treatment

parts.note: Vi is short for the girl's name Violet
carious describes teeth affected by decay, needing a dentist

explanation.surface: A substitute is needed because a girl must see the dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced or acting in place of someone else, a substitute's role.

clue.text: Provide food and drink when two queens meet?

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, and ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a queen is a female cat, and ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal hosting duty when two monarchs come together.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply meals and drinks, as for a party or event.

clue.text: Bemoans decentralised regulations

indicators.note: decentralised means losing the central letter

parts.note: regulations are rules

explanation.surface: Someone complains about regional regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret or lament something, a verb synonym in the same tense.

clue.text: A nice fresh start for businessman

indicators.note: start in the sense of jump or jerk suddenly, signalling the letters move around

explanation.surface: A businessman gets a pleasant new beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh start' looks like a unit, but 'fresh' is fodder and 'start' (jump) is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs a business under licence from a parent company.

clue.text: Steady partner, someone from same place

parts.note: steady means stable
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A dependable partner who comes from the same hometown.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a horse from the same stable, hence a colleague from the same organisation.

clue.text: It's faster than humans, and reportedly sharper

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: a sharper is a cheat or swindler, especially at cards

explanation.surface: Something quicker and cleverer than people.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is the fastest land animal, far outrunning any person.

clue.text: Dirty lad crossing ring road

indicators.note: crossing means the name spans the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: Sid is a boy's name
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A grubby boy crosses the ring road.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid or morally foul, a synonym for dirty.

clue.text: Less than honest during and after scripture lesson

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
since means after, as in 'since then'
RE is religious education, the school subject

explanation.surface: Someone is less than truthful in and after a religious class.
explanation.definitionFit: Not genuine or sincere, saying what one does not mean.

clue.text: Just receiving articles surreptitiously

indicators.note: receiving means taking another piece inside

parts.note: just means only
the definite article, made plural as several of them

explanation.surface: Someone merely takes in goods by stealth.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning secretly or furtively.

clue.text: Return shy setter's small token

indicators.note: return asks for everything that follows to be read back to front

parts.note: to shy is to throw or lob
the setter's means my, belonging to the person writing

explanation.surface: Sending back a modest gesture from a timid setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign or emblem representing something, as a token does.

clue.text: A carnal revel in Mediterranean resort

indicators.note: to revel is to make merry wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A sensual party in a Mediterranean holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal town and holiday destination on Cyprus.

clue.text: Clergyman meeting one element of Trinity in flesh!

parts.note: Ven. is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon
the Roman numeral for one is I
the Son is one of the three persons of the Trinity

explanation.surface: A cleric meets part of the Trinity in bodily form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in flesh' suggests incarnation; flesh is the definition, as in meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer meat, flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: Leave strychnine around part of church

indicators.note: around signals the answer lies in and about the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Poison left lying in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A room in a church where vestments are kept.

clue.text: Act of fiscal generosity? Ta!

parts.note: TA is a word for a levy with its last letter cut, and also British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A tax break prompts a quick thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: cut the end off a levy and you are left with TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Reducing taxation is a generous fiscal move by a government.

clue.text: A thousand thesauri differently expressed "inept"

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: differently expressed means the letters are put a different way

explanation.surface: Thesaurus entries offer other ways to say 'inept'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unskilled or clumsy, like a non-professional's work.

clue.text: Liberal dons having sex, not quite horizontally

indicators.note: dons is read as one piece being put on by another, so it ends up enclosed

parts.note: 'at it' is a slang euphemism for having sex

explanation.surface: Liberal university teachers being intimate, lying at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilted or tipped at an angle, so slanting slightly.

clue.text: Bank holiday without sign of life

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the words lie outside the answer, enclosing it

explanation.surface: A public holiday with no life in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian looped cross symbolising life.

clue.text: Madam regularly seen by A & E

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word Madam

explanation.surface: A lady at regular intervals visits the casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: A & E is a British hospital emergency department; here E is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: E is slang for ecstasy, the drug's chemical abbreviation.

clue.text: Go up to the bar with a mate

parts.note: to chin is to pull oneself up to a bar, as in a chin-up

explanation.surface: Head to the pub counter with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend.

clue.text: They cut minute out of The Archers, perhaps

indicators.note: out of means taken out from the following piece

parts.note: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in Ambridge, so its characters are Ambridgers

explanation.surface: Editors trim a minute from a radio soap episode.
explanation.definitionFit: People who shorten texts, condensing them.

clue.text: A brittle, cracked panel at top of window

indicators.note: cracked means broken apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A fragile, broken pane at the top of a window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer, the strip across the top of an app window showing its name.

clue.text: Graduate joining bank just a short while before

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate's degree
to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A graduate joined the bank only recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Only just, as in 'barely had he arrived when it rained'.
